1  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN  MACA.1464-2014  2  2025:KER:16358 FINALLY HEARD ON 06.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA.1464-2014  3  2025:KER:16358  JUDGMENT Dated this the 6th day of February, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1007/2006 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Alappuzha is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal) .
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 22.4.2006.

According to the petitioner, on 22.4.2006. at about 11 p.m., while he was riding a motor cycle, he was hit down by a Tata Sumo bearing registration No.KL-7T-799 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and 3 rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.9,62,750/-.

4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the MACA.1464-2014 2025:KER:16358 driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 to3 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A11.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.3.78,113/- and directed the insurer to pay Rajendran vs Mohammed Siraj on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13467443/
2 the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. Azad Babu, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. Lal Kl Joseph, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as manager in a Toddy shop and he is also a fisherman by profession, earning Rs.5,000/-.
per MACA.1464-2014 2025:KER:16358 month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.3,000/-.
He has also produced Exhibit A11 salary certificate and examined PW3 to prove the same.
From the evidence of Pw3, it is revealed that the petitioner is getting a monthly salary of Rs.5,000/- from the toddy shop.
Further according to him he is a fisherman by profession.
When the petitioner was examined as PW1, he claimed that apart from Rs.5,000/- received from the toddy shop, he used to get a sum of Rs.3,000/- per month from the fish farm maintained by him.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. It is true that the petitioner could not prove his income, as claimed in the OP.

However from Ext.
A11 salary certificate and from the evidence of PW3 it is proved that the petitioner was working as Manager in a toddy shop.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236],
the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2006 will come to Rs.5,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the evidence of PW1 that he used to get some income from his job as a fisherman also.
Therefore, his notional income is fixed at Rs.5,500/-.
12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:

MACA.1464-2014 2025:KER:16358 "T. fracture shaft femur (Rt) Type III C fracture shaft M/3rd - D/3rd junction, femur with medial condyle fracture (Rt) femur.
Type III C fracture B.B.(rt) leg."
13. He was treated as inpatient for a total period of 50 days.
As per Exhibit A10 disability certificate issued by PW2, Doctor, his permanent physical disability was assessed as

30%.The Tribunal,
however, without assigning any valid grounds rejected the disability certificate and proceeded to hold that the injuries sustained by the petitioner would affect his day to day activities of life and Rajendran vs Mohammed Siraj on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13467443/

sentences.text: 3 awarded a lump-sum amount of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'compensation for permanent disability'.
The above procedure adopted by the Tribunal is not correct as it is revealed that he sustained 30% permanent physical disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability as noted in Exhibit A10 is accepted and his disability is fixed as 30%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 46 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in MACA.1464-2014 2025:KER:16358 Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.3,21,750/-
15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs18,000/- being the income for 6 months @ Rs.3,000/-.

Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.5,500/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 33,000/- (5500x6months)
16.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.1,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 50 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.40,000/-, and 3,000/- respectively.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.6,96,863/-,

excluding interest for a period of 213 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal,
with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
